A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIN-FORCE study. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reflow, consolidation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original FIN-FORCE experiments in Table 2 and appendix Tables 15–16, a self-training iteration analysis in Figure 5, and a 500-sample human–LLM agreement study.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including Table 2, appendix Tables 14–15, Figure 5 and the human–LLM agreement results.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B.2 retain the same prompting, keyword replacement, fixed-noise sampling and SRLM self-training procedures. The generation and self-evaluation prompts also match after table renumbering.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,368 English financial headlines for evaluation and 2,105 supplementary headlines for training, with unchanged collection periods and risk/opportunity tasks. Category counts move from v1’s appendix Table 4 into v3’s Table 1; they do not represent expanded coverage.

E2.justification: The overall and risk/opportunity comparisons retain the same five LLMs under zero-shot and few-shot prompting, plus LLMs-for-CFs, CounterfactualDistil, LM-Counterfactuals and SRLM. Newly cited work in Section 2 is not added to the evaluated comparator set.

E3.justification: The reported model versions, generation and judging prompts, evaluation metrics, 500-sample human validation design, and SRLM training and selection settings are unchanged. Section 3.3 shortens the annotation-training description while retaining its 95% accuracy threshold.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the risk/opportunity comparison, few-shot effects, five qualitative error cases and four-iteration self-training analysis in Figures 2–5. No new ablation, robustness test or case study is reported.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging few-shot results over five random example samplings and original-headline perplexity over ten runs. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2, Figures 2–5 and the matched appendix result tables retain their values and findings. For example, LM-Counterfactuals remains at 65.50% FwdCompat-Dir Avg. and SRLM at 65.02%. Human agreement remains 81.4% for directionality and 89.6% for forward-compatibility.

T1.justification: The definitions and criteria for delta-perplexity, forward-compatibility and directionality remain equivalent. Neither version contains a formal theorem or proof contribution, and v3 adds no mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same benchmark contribution and principal findings: sampling-based generation performs best overall, self-training makes smaller models competitive, and existing methods retain important weaknesses. The scientific scope and novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The Limitations section adds a specific future direction: using forward counterfactuals to improve financial models’ explainability and performance, including stock prediction. The English-only limitation and interpretations of the experimental results are retained.

D1.justification: v1 promises release after review or acceptance; v3 states that the benchmark, supplementary data and experimental code are released and supplies a repository link in the abstract and Section 3.4. Implementation details remain unchanged. The PDFs establish this access-information change, not the repository’s contents.

R1.justification: Section 2 expands beyond NLP counterfactual benchmarks and generation methods to dedicated discussions of general counterfactual reasoning and financial LLM applications. It newly situates FIN-FORCE alongside stock prediction, financial statement analysis, ESG analysis and scenario-planning research, substantially broadening its literature coverage while retaining the central novelty claim.

P1.justification: v3 adds related-work subsections and acknowledgements, updates affiliations and contact details, and makes localized edits to annotation and metric explanations. Appendix benchmark statistics are consolidated into the main text; the overall organization and most scientific prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 merges the category counts from v1’s appendix Table 4 into main-text Table 1, expands Figure 1’s caption and reflows the document. Subsequent appendix tables are renumbered, while the result displays and other figures retain their content and design.

improvement.justification: v3 replaces deferred release promises with explicit access information, makes existing dataset-distribution counts visible in Table 1, and provides broader financial research context. These changes improve usability and contextual understanding. The methods, validation and reported results remain unchanged, so the supported overall gain is limited.
